pair_obstruction_atlas.consequence: Every atomic pair has an explicit collision class of size at least 5. Therefore no arbitrary deterministic 1-bit or 2-bit side channel can repair any atomic pair.

single_field_obstruction_atlas.consequence: Every atomic single-field base has an explicit collision class of size at least 33. Therefore no arbitrary deterministic 3-bit, 4-bit, or 5-bit channel can repair any single field.
single_field_obstruction_atlas.note: V90/V90.1 provide stronger exact/lower state bounds (best single e4 requires 57 states); the 33-graph atlas is a compact explicit obstruction sufficient for the 3..5-bit field-count lower bounds.

other_frontier_lower_bounds.0_bits: V75 exhaustively proves all atomic subsets of size <=4 incomplete; this lower bound is exhaustive-lattice based rather than represented by a single universal obstruction set.
other_frontier_lower_bounds.6_bits_zero_fields: With zero atomic fields, a 6-bit channel has at most 64 outputs for 12,005,168 graphs; counting alone rules out zero fields.

claim_scope: Exact finite n=10 obstruction atlas for the explicit deleted-card atomic family {e1..e9,tree}. Pair records preserve within-card field alignment. Impossibility consequences allow arbitrary deterministic side channels of the stated bit width. This is not a general graph-isomorphism or reconstruction theorem.
next_phase: Use this atlas together with V101 as the self-contained evidence layer for paper/reproducibility consolidation and literature/novelty calibration; do not resume serial full-catalog scans without a specific theorem gap.
